## STEP 6a — Embedding Strategy & Model Selection

*(Design only, no installation, no implementation)*

This step defines **how text chunks become searchable vectors**, **which models are appropriate**, and **why these choices strictly follow the project PDF constraints** .

---

## 1. Purpose of Embeddings in *This* Project

Embeddings exist **only for retrieval**, not for reasoning or answering.

In this project:

* **Chunks are retrieved via embeddings**
* **Answers are generated by an LLM**
* **Authority always stays with the source documents + human**

This separation is explicitly required because the PDF:

* treats AI as *probabilistic*
* requires *human review*
* forbids autonomous decision-making 

---

## 2. Where Embeddings Sit in the Pipeline

Current state (you already built this):

```
File → Document → Section → Chunk
```

After Step 6 (conceptually):

```
Chunk → Embedding → Vector Store → Retrieval
```

Important:

> **Embeddings never replace text.**
> They only point *to* text.

---

## 3. Design Requirements from the Project PDF

From the PDF, embeddings must satisfy:

1. **Local execution only**
2. **Open-source models**
3. **No cloud APIs**
4. **Deterministic & replaceable**
5. **Good performance on technical / legal text**
6. **Scales from laptop → workstation**

These are *non-negotiable* .

---

## 4. Embedding Granularity (Critical Decision)

### What we embed

✅ **Chunk text only**

### What we do NOT embed

❌ Section titles alone
❌ Entire documents
❌ Metadata-only records

Reason:

* Chunks are the **retrieval unit**
* Sections/documents are **citation parents**

This aligns with the Parent Document Retriever pattern you correctly identified earlier.

---

## 5. Embedding Model Selection — Design Criteria

We evaluate models on:

| Criterion         | Why it matters here        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------- |
| Language support  | Specs, contracts, policies |
| Domain neutrality | Not chat-optimized         |
| Vector size       | Memory & speed             |
| Local inference   | Mandatory                  |
| Community support | Debuggability              |

---

## 6. Recommended Model Class (Design-Level)

### ✅ Sentence-level embedding models (bi-encoders)

Not:

* chat models
* instruction-tuned LLMs
* generative models

**Why:**

* Fast
* Stable
* Retrieval-optimized
* Deterministic

---

## 7. Model Size Strategy (Important)

For this project (prototype → enterprise):

### Tiered approach (conceptual)

| Phase              | Model size   | Reason                 |
| ------------------ | ------------ | ---------------------- |
| Prototype (laptop) | Small–medium | Fast iteration         |
| Pilot              | Medium       | Better semantic recall |
| Production         | Medium–large | Higher accuracy        |

This mirrors the PDF’s **pilot → optimization → steady state** lifecycle .

---

## 8. Vector Characteristics (Design)

Typical embedding vectors will have:

* 384–1024 dimensions
* Float32 or Float16
* One vector per chunk

This is **small enough** for:

* local storage
* multiple role-based indexes
* incremental updates

---

## 9. Role-Based Embedding Separation (From PDF)

The PDF explicitly requires **role-based access via separate RAG vector databases** .

Design implication:

* Same embedding model
* **Different vector stores per role**
* Role filtering happens **before retrieval**

This avoids:

* leaking data
* complex permission logic inside prompts

---

## 10. What We Explicitly Do NOT Decide Yet

❌ Exact model name/version
❌ Exact library (FAISS / Chroma / etc.)
❌ Quantization
❌ GPU vs CPU
❌ Batch sizes

Those belong to **Step 6b / Step 7**.

Right now we only decide **what kind of model**, not *which binary*.

---

## 11. Why This Design Matches the Project PDF Perfectly

Because the PDF demands:

* traceable answers
* document-backed retrieval
* human validation
* local, open-source stack
* long-term optimization via better chunking & embeddings 

This embedding strategy supports all of that **without violating any constraint**.

---

## 12. One-Sentence Summary

> **We use local, open-source sentence embedding models to vectorize chunk text for retrieval only, keeping authority, traceability, and decisions strictly with documents and humans.**
